chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khash'ami, who said:

A group was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when a man from the adherents of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) entered, greeted him, sat down, and wept. Then he said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I made a vow to Allah that if He healed me from something I feared for myself, I would give in charity all that I own. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, healed me from it, and I have moved my family from my house to a tent among the ruins of the Ansar, and carried all that I own. So I am selling my house and all that I own to give in charity with it.'

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Go and evaluate your house, all your belongings, and whatever you own at a fair price, and note that. Then take a white parchment and write in it the total of what you have evaluated. Then look to the most reliable person in your eyes, hand over the parchment to him, bequeath to him, and instruct him that if death befalls you, he should sell your house and all that you own and give it in charity on your behalf. Then return to your house and manage your wealth as you were doing, so you and your family eat as you used to eat.'

Then consider everything you give in charity from what you are facing, whether in charity, maintaining kinship, or in aspects of righteousness, and write all of that down and count it. When the start of the year comes, go to the man to whom you bequeathed and instruct him to bring the parchment to you. Then write in it the total of what you gave in charity and spent on maintaining kinship or righteousness during that year. Then do that every year until you fulfill for Allah all that you vowed, and your house and wealth remain for you, if Allah wills.'
He said, and the man said, 'You have relieved me, O son of the Messenger of Allah! May Allah make me sacrificed for you.'

key_terms.عَهْدٌ: Vow or promise made to God

ai.seo_question: How to fulfill a vow of giving all wealth in charity without becoming destitute?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) resolves the dilemma of a man who vowed to donate all his wealth upon healing, offering a pragmatic solution that preserves the family's livelihood while fulfilling the vow. The Imam instructs him to appraise his assets, appoint a trustee to sell them posthumously, and gradually fulfill the vow through annual charitable expenditures, ensuring the total matches the initial valuation. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing spiritual commitment with practical economic stability, avoiding the rashness of immediate liquidation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad Bin Yahya Al Khash’amy who said, 
‘There was a group in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, when a man from the adherents of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> entered. So he greeted him<sup>asws</sup>, then was seated and cried. Then he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I gave a promise to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that if He<sup>azwj</sup> was to Heal me from something which I was afraid of upon myself, I would give in charity with the entirety of what I own; and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic did cure me from it, and I have transferred my family from my house to a canopy  from the ruins of the Helpers, and have carried every thing what I owned, so I would sell my house, and the entirety of what I own, so I would give in charity with it’. 
So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Go and evaluate your house, and the entirety of your belongings, and whatever you own with a just price, and recognise that. Then take to a white parchment and write down in it all of whatever you have evaluated. Then look around to a reliable one of the people with regards to yourself, so hand over the parchment to him, and bequeath to him and instruct him that if there were to occur an event with you, an event of the death, that he should sell your house and the entirety of whatever you own, so he should give it in charity with it on your behalf. Then return to your house, and evaluate upon what was in it. So consume, you and your family, similar what you used to consume. 
Then consider everything you give in charity with, with regards to what faces you from the charity, or helping the relatives, or in the aspects of righteousness, so write that down, all of it, and count it. So whenever it is the start of the year, so go to the man to whom you had bequeathed to, and instruct him that he should bring the parchment out to you. Then write in it the total of whatever you have given in charity, and the expenses upon your relatives, or righteous deeds during that year. Then keep on doing that during every year until you have fulfilled for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with the entirety of what you had vowed in it, and there would remain for you, your house, and your wealth, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘So the man said, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> have relieved me, O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Make me to be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 23. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath‘amiy who has narrated the following:

“Once we were with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in a group when a man came who was of the Mawali of abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He offered Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace), sat down, wept and said, I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause. I made a covenant with Allah that if He gives me recovery from my illness because of which I was afraid for my life, to give in charity all of my belongings and Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, granted me recovery from the illness. I have moved my family from my house to a ruined dome of al-Ansar (people of al- Madinah). I have carried all of my belongings and I am selling my house and all that I own to give them in charity.’

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘Go and appraise your house, all of your assets and belongings for a fair price and make it certain. Thereafter find a white sheet and write on it all that you have appraised, then find the most trustworthy person known to you among people arround you, then give the sheet to him and make a will. Instruct him that if something happened to you (death), to sell your house and all that belongs to you and give in charity on your behalf. Thereafter move back to your house to live as before with your family and maintain your family as before,

but make a list of what you spend and pay as charity, or gifts to relatives or for good causes, write them down all and calculate them. At the end of the year go to the executor of the will you have made and instruct him to deduct from the total on the list what you have spent as such for charity as mentioned in that year. Thereafter, every year you must do the same things until you fulfill all of what you had committed to do for Allah in the form of vow and commitment. In this way your house will remain for you as well as your other assets, if Allah so wills.’

The man then said, ‘You have released me from my entanglement, O child of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause.’”
